abstract: Spatial semantic segmentation of sound scenes (S5) jointly performs audio source separation and tagging on a multichannel audio mixture. Therefore, an S5 system can be decomposed into an audio tagging model and a separation model. The baseline S5 system in task~4 of the DCASE 2025 challenge uses M2D and ResUNet models for tagging and separation, respectively. These are large in overall size and therefore not appropriate for use in embedded devices. The main aim of this paper is to assess the performance loss in an S5 system when using lightweight tagging and separation models instead. To this end, we first compare the tagging performance of lightweight audio tagging models, namely PANNs and DyMNs, in terms of label prediction accuracy against the baseline M2D model. Secondly, we assess separation performance in terms of the scale-invariant signal-to-distortion ratio of the baseline ResUNet separator relative to that of a convolutional-based separator using SuDoRMRF. Finally, we combine the tagging and separation models across various configurations and assess the overall performance of the S5 system using the class-aware signal-to-distortion ratio.
